identity.name: United Belgian States
alt_names: Sovereign Congress of the United Belgian States

land.text: 'The United Belgian States ... coincided between 1789 and 1790 with the western and central part of present-day Belgium'; the other provinces 'except Luxembourg' followed Brabant

predecessors.note: Cliopatria draws these lands inside the Holy Roman Empire shape; the Habsburg Netherlands dossier of this batch holds the matching 1789-1790 contest and loss events with counterpart united-belgian-states.

land.text: 'by December the entire territory was again in imperial hands' (Surrender of Brussels, 2 December 1790)

successors.note: The Austrian Netherlands stay Habsburg until the French annexation of 1 October 1795 (page); that step belongs to habsburg-netherlands.

capitals.name: Brussels
capitals.note: Infobox 'Capital: Brussels'; 'The Sovereign Congress was seated in Brussels and consisted of representatives of each of the eight provinces.'

correction.text: the eight confederated provinces: Belgium without the Liege lands and without Luxembourg province

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (Cliopatria has no row for the confederation of 1790). The page gives no area and does not name the eight provinces; it says only that the state 'coincided between 1789 and 1790 with the western and central part of present-day Belgium' and that all provinces 'except Luxembourg' followed Brabant. Drawn as the gazetteer's Belgium minus the Liege province and minus the Luxembourg province (about 26,300 km2), soft. The Republic of Liege 'joined the United Belgian States in a semblance of an alliance' and is not drawn (rule 4: an alliance is not territory).

ledger.note: 11 January 1790: the confederation. 'On 11 January 1790 they signed a pact, establishing a confederation' of 'eight provinces' (infobox 'Treaty of Union: 11 January 1790'); the page: 'It existed from January to December 1790.' Brabant had declared itself independent first and 'all the other provinces of the Austrian Netherlands (except Luxembourg) soon followed suit'. The page does not name the eight.

region.text: the eight provinces of the confederation, Luxembourg province excepted

ledger.note: 24 October 1790: Namur. 'On 24 October 1790 imperial troops took the city of Namur.' The page speaks of the city; the province is the nearest unit the gazetteer has.

region.text: Namur province, retaken by the imperial army

ledger.note: 26 October 1790: West Flanders. 'Two days later, the province of West Flanders followed suit' (the day is counted from 24 October; the page gives no separate date).

region.text: West Flanders, retaken by the imperial army

ledger.note: 2 December 1790: Brussels surrenders (infobox 'Surrender of Brussels: 2 December 1790'); 'by December the entire territory was again in imperial hands', so the state ends. Entered as the loss of the remaining provinces.

region.text: the remaining provinces of the confederation, reconquered by Leopold II

wars.name: Brabant Revolution (1790 campaign)
wars.outcome: After Joseph II died (27 February 1790) Leopold II recaptured the territory: the Battle of Falmagne (22 September 1790, infobox), Namur on 24 October, West Flanders two days later and the surrender of Brussels on 2 December 1790; 'by December the entire territory was again in imperial hands'.
wars.note: The 1789 phase (Manifesto of Brabant 24 October 1789, Turnhout 27 October 1789) falls before this state; it is in the habsburg-netherlands dossier as a contest.

certainty.note: The page names no province but Brabant, Flanders and Namur, gives no area, and draws no boundary; the outline is the gazetteer's Belgium minus Liege and Luxembourg provinces.

sources.title: United Belgian States
sources.note: 11 January 1790 pact; eight provinces; Brussels; Namur 24 October 1790; West Flanders two days later; Brussels surrenders 2 December 1790.

notes:
Written 2026-10-25 for batch eu-09-x (1 page; budget 2-5). New state, type rebel: Cliopatria has no row for the confederation of 1790. It is a 11-month state, and the Habsburg Netherlands dossier of this batch carries the matching events (contest from the Battle of Turnhout, 27 October 1789; loss in January 1790; gain and contest end in December 1790) with counterpart `united-belgian-states`.

DATES FROM THE PAGE. 'On 11 January 1790 they signed a pact, establishing a confederation' (infobox 'Treaty of Union: 11 January 1790'); 'It existed from January to December 1790.' Infobox: Manifesto of Brabant 24 October 1789, Battle of Falmagne 22 September 1790, Surrender of Brussels 2 December 1790. 'On 24 October 1790 imperial troops took the city of Namur. Two days later, the province of West Flanders followed suit.' 'By December the entire territory was again in imperial hands.' The page also says Brabant 'declared that it no longer recognized the Emperor's rule' in 'January 1789' in its body, which contradicts the infobox's 24 October 1789 and the January 1790 treaty; I took the infobox dates and treat the body's 1789 as a slip of the page.

SHAPE. The page names no province but Brabant, Flanders and Namur, says all others 'except Luxembourg' followed, and gives 'the western and central part of present-day Belgium'. Drawn as gazetteer 'Belgium' minus the Liege province minus the Luxembourg province (about 26,300 km2). The Republic of Liege (1789-1791 on the page's timeline) 'joined the United Belgian States in a semblance of an alliance': not territory, so not drawn. The eight provinces are not named on the page.

NOT SETTLED. (1) The page says nothing of Ghent, Bruges, Mons or Tournai in 1790 and nothing of the Convention of The Hague (Habsburg-Dutch-British agreement of late 1790), so no event is entered for them. (2) Namur and West Flanders are entered as province-sized losses though the page speaks of 'the city of Namur' and 'the province of West Flanders'. (3) The Battle of Falmagne appears only in the infobox, undescribed. (4) The page gives no area or population.

COUNTERPARTS NEEDING DOSSIERS: none new (habsburg-netherlands is in this batch).
